lines.text: AI agents are already part of how companies work.
People ask them to read files, answer customers, write code, and move money.
But a language model is non-deterministic.
Ask the same thing twice, and the reasoning, the plan, even the action can change.
That's fine for a first draft. It's not fine for permissions.
So who decides what an agent may actually do? The model, or the company?
Betsee. Better see what your agents do, and deterministically control what they can do.
Your people keep the assistants they already use: Claude Code or Codex, inside Betsee Desk.
Every message is checked before the model sees it. Card numbers, IBANs, keys, and restricted names never leave.
Every tool call the assistant attempts goes to the Betsee Gateway first. If the Gateway can't be reached, nothing runs.
The Gateway decides every action in fifteen deterministic stages.
Identity, context, capability, Cedar policy, information tier, command validation, and budget.
AI analysis comes after policy, and it can only make a decision stricter.
Then approval, step-up, execution, and audit. Every stage is a span. Every decision is a trace.
Same conditions. Same policy. Same decision.
Run it again and again: the answer never changes. Change one real condition, and the decision changes predictably.
AI may tighten a decision. It can never silently loosen your boundary.
The Director shows your entire AI organization, live.
What needs attention right now. Every decision as it happens. And who touched what.
People, the agents they launch, and each agent's exact permissions: delegated by a person, intersected with policy.
Open any decision and follow it down: who asked, through which agent, for what, on which resource, and the exact rule that decided it.
High-impact actions wait for a human. The approver sees the exact action and parameters the Gateway recorded.
They prove who they are with a fresh one-time code. The approval becomes part of the context, and the same policy decides again.
In Policy Studio, business intent sits on top. Underneath, Cedar policies enforce it, before anything executes.
Sensitive data stays inside its boundary. A changed tool is blocked before any agent sees it.
A runaway agent hits its budget and is quarantined. And one agent can't borrow another agent's permissions.
Every control maps to a risk, and every decision leaves evidence.
Models will change. Agents will change. Your enterprise boundary remains yours.
Use AI, without handing control to AI.
Betsee. Non-deterministic AI. Deterministic control.
